experiment.claim: Issue #27 -- NOT a spec claim (spec/target-spec.md does not exist yet, spec/porting-plan.md Sec4 item 4). First characterization of the near-zero-Vt (native) NMOS device class this port introduced, which no sibling repo has data for and which spec/porting-plan.md Sec2.2/Sec2.6 explicitly defers to a characterization issue. Substantiates, per device flavor and per PDK bin geometry, at every point of the full 45-point PVT matrix: (a) constant-current threshold voltage and its process/temperature spread; (b) the drain current of a device wired exactly as design/por_output_chain.sch's MASSIST -- gate AND drain at VDD, source/bulk at VSS -- which is the always-on static current MASSIST costs in the released state and which design/por_output_chain.md records as uncharacterized and unbudgeted; (c) off-state (VGS=0) leakage at the same drain bias, for reference; (d) the supply voltage at which that MASSIST connection first sinks a stated assist current, i.e. the measurement behind por_output_chain.md's 'begins conducting from the very first millivolt of VDD' claim. The DUTs are bare PDK devices, not this design's cells: what is characterized here is the DEVICE menu, so the numbers feed the future por-iq spec row and the Sec2.6 flavor decision without making any claim about por_output_chain as a block. This experiment does NOT change the schematic and does NOT re-decide the flavor or the bin -- if the numbers say either should change, spec/decision-records/ owns that, per the issue's own out-of-scope list.
experiment.statistical_convention: N/A (deterministic corner-matrix characterization, not a distribution claim -- see notes: this experiment deliberately makes no statistical/yield claim, so it does NOT substitute for the Monte Carlo evidence sim/README.md keeps on a separate axis)
experiment.title: sky130 native-device characterization: nfet_05v0_nvt vs nfet_03v3_nvt threshold voltage, MASSIST-condition static current, off-state leakage and assist-onset voltage over the full PVT matrix

spread_checks.note: Corner-blindness guard, same house convention as sim/bias-core-smoke/'s vref spread check: native-device Vth is strongly process- and temperature-dependent, so if every corner returns the same threshold the .lib corner / .temp injection is not reaching the models and the whole matrix is one point repeated 45 times.

Second corner-blindness guard on the headline measurement itself. ion_n05l25 must additionally vary along the SUPPLY axis (VGS = VDS = 'vsup'), which vth_n05l25 by construction does not -- so this check covers the .param vsup injection, which the vth spread check cannot.
